title: spatial-failover-hedge-prevent-double-evictions-and-slo-race
author: Eleanor Grant
description: Background: During a multi-region failover exercise we observed a race where two independent failover coordinators would concurrently mark the same tenant slots for eviction. That caused: 1) duplicate eviction operations that shortened SLO budget windows twice for affected tenants; 2) kv-cache drain attempts that raced and triggered connection churn; 3) alert storms and automated throttles firing incorrectly. Root cause: eviction intent was propagated via soft signals and local timers; there was no single serialized lease for eviction intent across the spatial (multi-region) mesh. Motivation: prevent tenants from being 'double-penalized' during cross-region failover events, reduce churn during probe jitter, and make SLO accounting idempotent when failover actions overlap. Changes in this PR: 1) introduce a lightweight control-plane lease called the "spatial failover hedge" (SFH). SFH is an ephemeral, short TTL lease that must be acquired before an eviction intent is committed. 2) add a soft serialized handoff path: if a coordinator cannot acquire SFH immediately it records intent and performs a probabilistic backoff (configurable) instead of immediate eviction. 3) decouple SLO debit from eviction execution by moving SLO bookkeeping to a single control-plane actor that only records a debit when SFH-lease-based eviction is observed to start. 4) add a duplicate-eviction detector metric and alert (eviction.intent.duplicate_attempts) and a k/v drain quiet-window to avoid connection storms. 5) a small CLI toggle (control-plane feature flag) and a rollout plan with canary by region. Files changed are isolated to the control plane coordination, one runtime guard, and observability plumbing (see files_changed). Testing and validation: - unit tests for lease acquisition and TTL behavior (control-plane/lease_test.go) - e2e canary in staging with synthetic failover (pipeline: e2e-failover-canary) - load tests showing SLO debit rate goes down under overlapping failover scenarios (bench/perf/overlap-sim) - manual rollback path validated by flipping the feature flag to off and verifying no eviction/lease mutations occur. Rollout plan: 1) enable SFH in staging for 24h and run e2e canary; 2) canary enable in us-west-2 with 5% traffic for 6 hours and monitor duplicate_attempts, evictions/sec, and slo-debits; 3) progressive region-by-region enable over 48 hours if metrics stable. Rollback: feature flag off; revert control-plane schema change (small migration is idempotent) if unexpected issues. Related: references ENG-4821 (SLO accounting hardening) and SUP-1298 (customer incident correlation). Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] e2e canary - [x] docs: brief note in reliability-runbook.md - [x] telemetry and alerts added - [x] feature-flag gated for safe rollback

release_notes: Hotfix: introduce spatial failover hedge to serialize eviction intent across regions, preventing duplicate evictions and incorrect SLO debits during overlapping failovers. Adds new metric eviction.intent.duplicate_attempts and a control-plane feature flag for staged rollout.
notes_for_operators: When enabling via feature flag set rollout:region canary percentage to 0 initially. Watch eviction.intent.duplicate_attempts and slo.debits.rate for regressions. If evictions stall after enabling, flip feature flag off; the control-plane migration is safe to revert.
post_merge_actions: 1) Deploy control-plane with feature flag off to prod; 2) Enable canary region per rollout plan; 3) monitor dashboards and alerts for 24h; 4) file follow-up to replace probabilistic backoff with lease-requeue when cluster-wide consensus is available (ENG-4923).
